provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft; host source restrictions and execution verification

draft_notes.explanation: The mechanism (full row+column cross through each seed, the 4 diagonal neighbours marked, seed recoloured) is invariant under every D4 transform: rows map to rows or columns, columns to the other, and the diagonal-neighbour set maps onto itself. So no direction needs rewriting; the emitted program works directly in visible coordinates on any rectangular grid. Only colour roles are specialised: line colour = palette[1], centre = palette[2], diagonal marker = palette[3]. Background is the most common colour; seeds are every non-background cell. The drawing order (crosses, then diagonals, then centres) matches the archived solver; the generator rejects scenes in which a diagonal marker or centre would be overwritten by another seed's line, so the order is consistent with the constructor's domain. Diagonal markers that fall outside the grid are dropped.
draft_notes.limitations: This assumes the background is the strict majority colour, which holds because the generator places at most about 6 seeds on an 8-16 square grid. It also assumes every non-background cell in the input is a seed. Outside the generator's no-clobbering domain, the program follows the archived priority (centre over diagonal over line). The fixtures show no contradictions with the rule. I have not run any tests on this factory.
